//: The decisions a modernization cannot make from the code. scripts/decisions.mjs fills in `evidence` and `suggested` for one package. The owner answers; the agent does not.

questions.question: The public API takes error-first callbacks. What happens to them?
questions.when: the survey finds error-first callbacks outside the tests

options.label: Drop
options.meaning: async/await only. A function passed where the callback used to go is ignored. Quiet for a caller who missed the migration.

options.label: Throw
options.meaning: async/await only. A function passed where the callback used to go throws a TypeError that names the promise form. Loud.

options.label: Support both
options.meaning: Return a promise and still honour a trailing callback. Costs an adapter on every method and a union in every signature.

options.label: Keep callbacks
options.meaning: Callbacks only, no promises. Rare, and right when callers depend on synchronous-callback timing or the package sits under other callback code.

questions.question: Which module system does the package ship?

options.label: ESM only
options.meaning: One build. CommonJS callers load it through require() of an ES module on current Node.

options.label: Dual
options.meaning: ESM and CommonJS builds. The owner names the build tool.

options.label: CommonJS only
options.meaning: Stay on CommonJS and modernize everything else.

questions.question: What is the Node.js floor?
questions.note: Only release lines supported on the day of the work are offered. Look them up in the Node.js release schedule. A floor on an unsupported line is refused.

options.label: Oldest supported line
options.meaning: Widest reach. That line may leave maintenance during this major.

options.label: Active LTS
options.meaning: Supported for the likely life of this major.

options.label: Current
options.meaning: Newest features, narrowest reach.

options.label: JSDoc, declarations generated
options.meaning: JavaScript source, checked JSDoc, .d.ts emitted at publish. One source of truth.

options.label: JSDoc, checked only
options.meaning: JSDoc is typechecked in CI and no declarations ship.

options.label: Hand-written .d.ts
options.meaning: Declarations beside the source, with the conformance gates in references/type-gates.md.

options.label: Migrate to TypeScript
options.meaning: Source becomes .ts. The owner names how it is built or run.

options.label: No types
options.meaning: Leave types to DefinitelyTyped or to nobody.

options.label: Biome
options.meaning: Lint and format in one tool.

options.label: oxlint
options.meaning: Lint only. The owner names a formatter or goes without.

options.label: node:test
options.meaning: No dependency.

options.label: Keep what is there
options.meaning: Only offered when the current runner is maintained.

questions.question: Which runtimes must it run on?

options.label: Node.js, Bun and Deno
options.meaning: No Node-only APIs without a guard. CI runs each.

options.label: Servers and browsers
options.meaning: No node: imports in the entry graph.

questions.question: What happens to dependencies the platform has absorbed?

options.label: Replace with built-ins
options.meaning: The helpers they provided become this package's code and need tests.

options.label: Upgrade in place
options.meaning: Keep each one, on its current major.

questions.question: The baseline found defects in the old version. Fix them in this major?
questions.when: Step 1 pinned behaviour that is plainly a bug

options.label: Fix and list them
options.meaning: Each is a row in the migration guide.

options.label: Preserve
options.meaning: Bug-for-bug. Fixes come in a later release.

options.label: Parity only
options.meaning: The old surface in the new dialect. Nothing new.

options.label: Only where the language caught up
options.meaning: New API when a language feature changes what the package is for.

questions.question: Callers could import any file. What stays importable?

options.label: Entry points only
options.meaning: An exports map with the documented entries. Deep imports throw.

options.label: Keep the old paths
options.meaning: An exports subpath for each file callers are known to import.

options.label: No exports map
options.meaning: Everything stays importable.

options.label: Prepare, do not release
options.meaning: Version commit and instructions. The owner tags and publishes.

options.label: Prerelease first
options.meaning: Publish under a `next` tag before `latest`.

questions.question: Does the previous major keep getting fixes?

options.label: No
options.meaning: The old major is done. Say so in the README.

options.label: Security fixes only
options.meaning: Keep a maintenance branch.

options.label: Deprecate it on the registry
options.meaning: With a pointer to the new major.
